New Thought
noo thawt
noun phrase (a metaphysical movement)
A nineteenth-century American metaphysical movement teaching the creative power of the mind and positive thinking; a chief root of the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith teaching.

Biblical Definition

New Thought is a nineteenth-century American metaphysical and mind-cure movement, arising from the teaching of Phineas Quimby and spread through figures and groups such as Mary Baker Eddy's Christian Science, the Unity School, and the “positive thinking” popularizers, holding that the mind possesses creative power, that thoughts shape reality, that sickness and poverty arise from wrong thinking, and that man may attain health, wealth, and well-being by the right use of his mental and spiritual powers. The dictionary names New Thought as a serious corruption and, in its developed forms, a counterfeit religion. It denies the biblical doctrine of God, man, sin, and salvation, putting in the place of the sovereign Creator an impersonal divine principle, and in the place of the fallen sinner needing redemption a divine self needing only enlightenment. The apostle's warning fits it exactly: “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men… and not after Christ”; for these are the vain babblings and oppositions of science falsely so called. New Thought exalts the thoughts of man, when the LORD declares, “My thoughts are not your thoughts.” The dictionary marks its lasting and dangerous legacy within the church: New Thought is a principal root of the prosperity gospel and the word-of-faith movement, which baptize its mind-power doctrine in Christian language—teaching that faith is a force, that positive confession creates reality, that the believer may command health and wealth by speaking the word. These the dictionary identifies as New Thought in Christian dress, corrupting the simplicity that is in Christ as the serpent beguiled Eve. Over against the whole system the dictionary holds the gospel: man is a fallen sinner, not a latent god; salvation is by the grace of God in Christ, not by the power of the mind; and reality is shaped not by human thought but by the Word of the God whose thoughts are higher than ours.

Webster 1828 Definition

A 19th-century metaphysical movement (Quimby, Christian Science, “positive thinking”) teaching the creative power of the mind; a counterfeit religion and the chief root of the prosperity and word-of-faith gospels that dress its mind-power doctrine in Christian language.

NEW THOUGHT, noun phrase. A 19th-century American metaphysical and mind-cure movement.

Arose from Phineas Quimby; spread through Christian Science, Unity, and “positive thinking.”

Teaches that thoughts shape reality and that mind-power yields health and wealth.

A counterfeit religion denying the biblical God, man, sin, and salvation.

The chief root of the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith teaching.

Key Scripture

Col 2:8 — "Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ."

Isa 55:8 — "For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD."

1 Ti 6:20 — "O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called:"

2 Co 11:3 — "But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ."

Modern Corruption

New Thought is itself the corruption: a counterfeit religion of mind-power that denies the biblical God, man, sin, and salvation, and whose Christianized offspring are the prosperity and word-of-faith gospels.

expand to see more

New Thought is the corruption to be named, not a doctrine at risk of drift. It is a metaphysical religion of mind-power, teaching that thoughts create reality, that the divine is an impersonal principle to be tapped, and that man attains health and wealth by right thinking. The dictionary names it a counterfeit of the faith. It replaces the sovereign personal God with a force, the fallen sinner with a latent god needing only enlightenment, and salvation by grace with self-improvement by mental technique. The apostle's words mark it exactly: it spoils men through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men and not after Christ, the vain babblings and oppositions of science falsely so called.

The dictionary presses especially its legacy within the professing church. New Thought is the principal root of the prosperity gospel and the word-of-faith movement, which take its mind-power doctrine and dress it in Christian language: faith becomes a creative force, “positive confession” becomes a means of commanding reality, and the believer is taught to speak health and wealth into being. The dictionary identifies these as New Thought in Christian clothing, corrupting the simplicity that is in Christ as the serpent beguiled Eve. Over against the whole scheme it sets the gospel: man is a sinner needing redemption, not a god needing enlightenment; salvation is by God's grace in Christ, not by the power of the mind; and the LORD's thoughts, not man's, govern reality, for His thoughts are not our thoughts.

Hebrew Roots

From the “new thought” of mind-power and positive thinking; rooted in Phineas Quimby's mind-cure, spread through Christian Science, Unity, and the prosperity gospel.
